main_body: A flat grass ground patch (4x3 tiles) with repeating darker tufts and light-green sprout clumps; terrain tile, not a standing object
top_band: none - terrain ground texture, no standing volume
evidence: The image is a seamless grass ground patch, not a standing object. There is no top surface or front face to judge, so the 3/4 contract does not apply. Nothing in it is drawn as a front elevation, a side elevation or a top-down slab. Terrain kind matches.

style.evidence: The patch uses about 5 greens: a dark tuft, a deep shadow, a mid base, a light sprout and a bright highlight. It has no outlines. The base is dotted with sparse darker pixels, so there are no large flat areas. The tufts repeat in an obvious grid, one per tile, which makes it look patterned and tiled. Each tile carries roughly 6-8 colours, a bit below the richer reference grass tiles. It is acceptable next to the grass reference, though a little more mechanical than hand-varied Beodeul grass. The mid-green base is very close in value to the dots, so the texture reads low-contrast but present.
